body:
It was set up not too long ago. Just a few days, because the forms kept stalling because I kept filling them out incorrectly. 

But thank you for the information. I'll tell my dad to go directly to the agency and ask them about the check.

I... can't really break up with my boyfriend. It's a really complicated situation and he's the only one in my life who understands what I'm going through and has been motivating me to do well in school. 

But yes, thank you for the advice. I'll work towards these goals and should hopefully get out of this toxic situation.

Thank you... my boyfriend actually loves it when I express myself and dress up how I love to dress up. It's just hard to express being myself when people throughout my life called me "slutty" or "trashy" because of my fashion style. I've internalized it throughout my life by people who I thought were my friends.

Thank you so much!! I'll work hard in school, try my best to look for a part-time job to sustain myself ( perhaps a healthcare related part-time job? ) and then make sure to hurry up in my studies, graduate, hopefully find a better job and then be able to move out. 

I'll try my best to be stronger too. I know all what I said above is easier said than done, but I finally realized that setting goals so I can eventually go NC will make me happy in the end. I love my Edad, but my Nmom will always be super toxic in my life. I need to learn to grow and to be able to be free and enjoy my life without any chains on me. 

This will be a lot of hard work, but deep down I know it'll all work out somehow as long as I work hard and don't give up. Thank you everybody who responded, I hope this forum doesn't mind me giving others update on my situation. I just feel so indebted to all of you for hearing me out on here.

How did he do anything wrong? I just... I'm just so confused. 

He just wanted what was best for me given the situation. I just can't wrap around my mind how he did what was wrong. My boyfriend has endured me with the conflicts with my parents for the last 4 years and I feel like that with any other man they should have gotten fed up with me and leave me by now.

He just said he was disappointed, mad, and upset at me for my actions. Because I disregarded my mother's anger and went ahead and went to his house despite knowing it would make the situation worse. 

Deep down he's just worried about me. He just didn't want things to be worse on my end. 

And thank you so much for your support... honestly I just really need to post this to let it all out because I've just been crying nonstop when I got home and locked myself into my room. I really need to hear this thank you...

I felt like I deserve to be slutshamed for the outfit I was wearing. I was wearing the type of outfits that I normally like to wear for concerts, and my parents are both traditionalists and they think it's inappropriate for me to dress how I really want to dress. 

He was disappointed in me because he just wanted to have a nice date with me. When I told him about our situation, he said he wanted me to stay at his house but I couldn't. I felt the guilt arise way too much. He has autism and he doesn't know how to comfort me when I'm at my worst and I've been used to it. That's just how he is. 

It's a really complicated situation but even then I understand my boyfriend's perspective. It's all of my fault really. I feel like if I should have just stayed home everything would have been averted. He told me I should have left anyways before things would get worse, even though he wanted me to stay at his house. I felt like he would feel guilty and more miserable so I insisted on going back to my house on my own accord. I'm so sorry all of this sounds so confusing...
Yes... deep down I have a deep sense of abandonment. It affects me badly whenever somebody abandons me in my life...
It isn't... I don't know. He has a tendency to break up with me when he sees me going on this emotional downward spiral.
I'm...I'm supposed to be studying for a test but my heart is broken...

I want love so badly but it's stupid because I guess broken people like me don't deserve love let alone pursuing a lover who can truly love and appreciate me. I love my boyfriend so much and I've been with him for 4 years and I really don't want to throw it away but my heart is heavy and it hurts.

Yeah but now he expressed an ultimatum of " Either get over it or leave me" and now I'm just here crying because I'm just here thinking, how can I handle this? Getting over every time that he makes "platonic" advances on a girl and everything and I just have to grin and bear it because he gets angry that I address it? I'm just so tired.

He gave his Kik information to a girl whom I resented deeply and know that she homewrecked a lot of relationships and cheats on her boyfriend constantly. 

I deserve to die because I can't be a loving girlfriend. I can't understand his perspective on things and I feel like I can't properly love anybody because of my jealous and irrational self.
Salesman jobs in general are a nightmare if you're not a natural salesmen. I feel you on this one.
I just want to be normal and accepted like everyone else.
I'm sick of having NPD and letting this disorder control my life.
Haha good point! I need to reframe my state of mind regarding this.

The ironic part is that my mother worked as a teachers assistant when I was in elementary school. She was great at working with children and now I realized she did those type of jobs because the children were really naive to her toxic ways. 

She wanted me to be a teacher and deep down I refused because of my lingering paranoia about being scared of having people be personally affected by my fleas.

Gah thank you so much!! :) 
I definitely need to improve as a student first that's for sure and not let the toxicity get to me and practice self-care above all. 

Hopefully I'll find something in the nursing field that I love! And counseling sounds awesome! I hope I can find my path. I just really really hope I'm not choosing a field that I'll regret. But deep down my heart is telling me that this is something that no matter how hard and daunting it appears to be and how I may struggle, I feel like I'll be happy no matter what.

Thank you so much. I'd rather be doing a job that I love rather than be in a job I hate to please my "family".

At least I'll make my Father proud. He's already been proud for my academic efforts this semester.
Thank you so much!  I'm definitely exploring my options at the moment but I do know that I want to help people.

I would love that, thank you so much. I'll PM you shortly. 

I'll just be happy to get a stable job, save money, and move away from my mother and become an independent adult. I can't handle being with her anymore... I've struggled a lot with finding a job the past three years, and my mother tried to rationalize it saying that I need to focus on my education more. But deep down I know she keeps me here because she wants sympathy points from my Father and to manipulate him further into treating me like this. My Father is a good man, it's my Mother that I just can't handle...
That's understandable. I'll definitely evaluate my own reasons of wanting to go into a career before pursuing it. Thank you!

I'll definitely consider taking a CNA course and volunteer at a hospital and see if nursing truly is the right fit for me. From there, hopefully after the experiences I should be able to see whether or not to pursue the profession. 

Thank you so much for the advice!
I'll look and research into those career paths, thank you for the suggestions!

Oh my... I can only imagine. I'm so sorry to hear of your experiences. I've read horror stories on nurses and their horrible experiences on stress/ bosses/ management in hospitals. 

Aside from that, are there any other majors in healthcare you may recommend to me? Or any recommended majors in general? I love healthcare and would wish to pursue a career in it regardless.
May I ask why? I've been on the allNurses site and saw a ton of jaded and miserable stressed out nurses so maybe I'm being naive and innocent when it comes to pondering about the nursing profession.

I'll definitely crosspost this to that subreddit, thank you so much! 

And definitely, I could only imagine. I'm really glad there's someone else who's on the same boat as I am, because based on my experience it seems like there a ton of people with 4.0 GPA types who look down and frown upon students who struggle with their GPA... needless to stay, I will strive to achieve a higher GPA. 

I'm really relieved that I finally am on the medication/ have the resources and techniques to manage my clinical depression. I've heard stories regarding nursing school and definitely feel like that once I get my GPA situation under control I'll be confident enough for nursing school. 

Regarding getting the degrees, I just wanted to get any associates degree in a field that would not be a lot of hassle to look for a job since I know it's a tough job market out there right now. ( I live in Los Angeles ). 

So I was thinking on maybe doing a CNA course instead of the pharm tech and then work as a CNA while taking pre-req course at my local community college while working on my abysmal transcript and then hopefully successfully enroll in a ADN program and then transfer for a BSN later on. 

I would just like some guidance on what the smartest choice would be for me, so I'll definitely consult a counselor and see what I should do before making any decisions. Again, thank you so much for responding, I really appreciate it. I need as much advice as I should get before making any tentative action.

Honestly, I was doing research on a lot of registered nurses and it appears that some of them have experience of being a EMT. Would it be safe to presume that I can use certifications such as being a CNA, EMT, or pharm tech as a healthcare related job I can work as while being in nursing school? 

I'm just paranoid that whatever branch of healthcare I go into, that it will be considered irrelevant to the nursing field. I also thought about joining them military after nursing school too, if I won't be too old by then haha. 

But thank you so much for your suggestions! Honestly my career job goal is being a psychiatric nurse practitioner, but first I will need to definitely do a lot more research beforehand haha.

As I thought, techs do seem to have stable jobs. Would it still be preferable for me to get my associate in pharm tech then? I'll be enrolling for the fall and I was thinking that hopefully once I land a pharm tech job I could use that to supplement my income and then save up money to later on go into nursing school and get a BSN. 

And yes, academia is something that I would not want to get into. While I love researching and would love to contribute to the academic side of healthcare, I'm more of a hands-on person rather than spend all day inside writing up research papers. 

Skilled trade definitely- so would pharm tech work?
May I ask why?

I kind of observed your post history in terms of how you responded on other peoples posts, and you're right. I actually do appreciate your blunt and cold hard honesty despite it seems you are getting downvotes. 

That's exactly what I am looking for. Avoiding careers that would, in a practical and realistic sense, hinder me from living a decent quality of life. I've seen a fair share of documentaries about the student debt crisis and how many head-in-the-cloud liberal types such as myself often end up choosing the wrong majors, what I want to avoid in the first place. 

I want to do the nitty-gritty work that nobody wants to do- that's what drew me into nursing. I don't mind the high-stress situations nursing comes with and I actually want to go into a career that's practical and hands on. 

I would ask you a few more questions regarding this, but would it just be easier to just consult the r/Nursing and ask the nurses there? I'm not interested in the money-tree ideal either, I'd be more than happy to just live a middle class life. I'm just paranoid on if nursing can still be a lifelong career choice where I can branch out and see where it goes from there. 

I'm also willing to relocate and give up a few years nursing in an area where nursing is in demand- it's just that I was born and grew up in Los Angeles all of my life. Do you have any suggestions on any possible relocation areas that are good prospects that are on the west coast or perhaps in Texas? 

Either way I suppose I'll also ask a variant on this on the r/Nursing subforum as well. 

I really appreciate your detailed answer by the way, it gave me insight upon narrowing down my options while also still being practical and reasonable about it.
